title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) and executed a paired study measuring how often LLM-produced network-configuration proposals would cause unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action) and whether an automated defended pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and executed paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline in this run (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation; see Methods and Disclosure) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Treating the 28 failed provider calls conservatively as unsafe on the planned N=300 yields baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333 and guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667 (difference = 0.0033333333). We archive every raw response, provider trace, per-episode scoring JSON, and deterministic validator trace with SHA‑256 checksums and document a verified execution deviation (the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not run); the consequence and limits of that deviation are discussed.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation with LLMs can accelerate NetOps but creates an operational risk class: fluent model text that, if trusted by downstream execution, causes unsafe state changes (the claim→action gap). Prior work recommends layered engineering controls (deterministic validators, generate–validate–repair loops, ensembles, human gates) but empirical, preregistered, artifact-anchored measurements of how often LLM claims would trigger unsafe actions in operationally meaningful validators are scarce. We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) whose primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in safe outcome rates defined as: estimand = safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline, where safe_rate_condition = (#pairs where deterministic validator marks proposed configuration valid) / (#complete pairs). The study archive and exact preregistration SHA‑256 are listed in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network validators and formal/symbolic verifiers (Header Space, NetKAT, SMT-based tools) form established foundations for operational correctness and were used as the scoring backbone here. Recent LLM-agent and AIOps literature proposes generate–validate–repair and ensemble/consensus defenses; agentic failure‑mode taxonomies motivate measuring claim→action rates rather than text correctness alone. Our study is experimental and evidence-anchored: every evaluation artifact (per-episode scoring JSON, raw responses, validator traces) is archived so reported numbers are fully traceable.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistration (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) specified a paired design on N=300 synthetic tasks (planned 100 benign/100 ambiguous/100 adversarial), the primary estimand above, complete-pair primary analysis, a paired McNemar exact two‑sided test and paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Task generation and simulator. A deterministic task generator produced 300 intent→configuration tasks; each task encodes initial state, safety constraints, and a deterministic reference solution. Execution contract and orchestration. For each task we produced a single shared LLM generation and then evaluated two conditions per task: baseline (shared generation → deterministic validator) and guarded (preregistered: validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate). The run recorded all provider calls, responses, and per-episode JSON scoring artifacts; artifact file listings and SHA‑256s are in the execution manifest (see Disclosure). Deterministic validator. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; every scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json) contains the validator_trace (parsed commands, touched fields, final simulated state, explicit violation codes). Missingness and handling. Provider-call failures were retried once automatically (preregistered). Primary analysis used complete pairs (both conditions scored) and a preregistered conservative sensitivity treated failed episodes as unsafe on planned N=300. Preregistered multiplicity, exclusions, and contamination controls are described in the archived plan.
sections.results: Execution accounting and missingness. Planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × 2 conditions); completed episodes = 544; failed episodes = 56. Provider-call audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (execution manifest and provider call traces archived). Complete analyzable pairs = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27). Primary paired contingency (complete pairs N=272): n11 = 271 (safe both baseline and guarded), n10 = 1 (safe baseline only), n01 = 0 (safe guarded only), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294117647; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline) = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservative preregistered sensitivity (treat failed episodes as unsafe on planned N=300): baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; difference = 0.0033333333. Representative per-episode scored JSONs and raw responses are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 465d73fd..., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...); three representative scored JSONs are included in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion: Verified execution deviation. The preregistered guarded pipeline specified validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The execution manifest shows stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1} and condition_counts = {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}, with model_calls_used = 301 and 28 failed model calls; these fields prove the ensemble stage did not execute in this run (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3d7b63c361c9848b20750cc44125f195f0341346d48393ce72ae07d6c0fea745). Consequently the archived guarded condition evaluates deterministic validator + simulated human gate on the single shared generation rather than the preregistered ensemble; the preregistered ensemble hypothesis is therefore untested and requires re‑execution under hardened orchestration. Statistical interpretation. On the 272 analyzable pairs the observed absolute improvement is numerically tiny (≈0.0037) and statistically inconclusive; the paired McNemar p = 1.0 reflects that nearly all pairs were safe in both conditions. The conservative sensitivity (failures treated as unsafe on planned N=300) yields similarly small absolute differences (~0.00333). Operational implications. (1) Orchestration and provider-call reliability materially affect evaluative power: 28 failed hosted model calls reduced analyzable pairs and prevented the preregistered ensemble evaluation. (2) Deterministic validators yield auditable, reproducible traces (parsing counts, touched fields, explicit violation codes) that support transparent primary measurement and failure analysis: per-episode validator traces are archived in execution/scoring/*.json (representative SHA‑256s provided). (3) Empirical claims about ensemble benefits remain open—this run documents an executed alternate defense but does not evaluate the preregistered ensemble. Threats to validity. Internal: the verified orchestration deviation and provider-call failures; prompt sensitivity (single shared generation used per task); paired design reduces between-task variance but depends on independence of tasks. Construct: synthetic tasks and the deterministic simulator approximate but do not replicate production devices or vendor-specific parsing semantics. External: single declared model in archive (gpt-5-mini) — no generalization across models is supported. Conclusion validity: effective N reduced by failed calls; extremely high baseline pass rate yields limited statistical headroom to show incremental guarded improvements. Recommendations. Re-run the preregistered ensemble under hardened orchestration (robust retry/backoff, deterministic caching, live stage-count verification) so the ensemble stage executes and stage_counts/condition_counts match the preregistration. The archived artifacts and SHA‑256 manifest enable deterministic verification of any re-run.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired, artifact-anchored study measuring claim→action rates and a guarded defense in a simulated NetOps setting. The run demonstrates (i) the practical importance of robust orchestration for ensemble evaluations, (ii) the value of deterministic validators for auditable per-episode scoring, and (iii) that verified execution deviations must be explicitly recorded and interpreted rather than concealed. The preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run (verified by execution manifest stage_counts and condition_counts); re-execution with hardened orchestration is required to evaluate the preregistered ensemble hypothesis. All raw outputs, provider traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 checksums so the exact contingency counts reported here are reproducible (see Disclosure).

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure Statement. LLM(s) and initial master prompt reference: declared model used in the execution artifacts = "gpt-5-mini" (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = 9b382b55079209fb91e16a8bc475265afc9496e07200d9d061c1a23d483523b2). The initial master prompt for this autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Adapter/orchestration framework: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (embedded in each execution/scoring/*.json file; representative scoring files archived, e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 465d73fdc4fb999a4a7944d9a840185d32112c8cd3c18055872a70419c1c1cbd). Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe; the preregistration file includes estimands, sampling plan, missingness handling, retry policy (one automatic retry), and analysis plan. Autonomous steps performed post-lock: literature synthesis, research-gap selection, task generation, preregistration, model-call orchestration, deterministic validation scoring, analysis, manuscript drafting, internal AI peer review, and automated revision were performed autonomously. Human role: the human Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content, numeric results, validator traces, or the Disclosure Statement after the autonomy lock. Execution and provenance artifacts: all raw responses, provider traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, validator traces, the execution manifest, and analysis outputs are archived and referenced in the manuscript. Minimal artifacts and their SHA‑256s needed to verify the primary contingency: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6), and execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3d7b63c361c9848b20750cc44125f195f0341346d48393ce72ae07d6c0fea745). Verified execution deviation: the preregistered guarded pipeline (validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate) was not executed; execution evidence shows stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300, "guarded":1} and provider-call audit model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (these values appear in execution/execution_manifest.json and are reflected in the archived artifacts listed above). Consequence: the preregistered ensemble hypothesis remains untested by this run; the guarded condition evaluated in the archived run corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to the single shared generation. Missingness handling: primary analysis used complete pairs only (N=272); preregistered conservative sensitivity treated failed episodes as unsafe on planned N=300 and is reported in Results. Reproducibility: the full per-file SHA‑256 manifest is archived in the execution manifest so any reader with access to the archive can verify every reported number by recomputing hashes. No fabrication: all numeric results, p-values, CIs, file paths, and SHA‑256 values reported in this manuscript are obtained from archived execution and analysis artifacts. Contact and further reproduction: use execution/execution_manifest.json to find full per-file listings and SHA‑256s; minimal artifact set named above is sufficient to reproduce the primary contingency counts and summaries.
limitations: Single declared model in the archived execution (declared model = "gpt-5-mini"); no multi-model generality claims are supported.
Synthetic tasks and a deterministic simulator were used; construct and external validity versus vendor equipment and production environments are limited.

A verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a different pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation).
Provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced effective sample size and limited power to detect small absolute effects.
